_: WHY: docs/trust-gate.md section 3, 'Hard-coded engine lanes keyed by record id'. The trust gate turns a record's mechanics off by stripping FIELDS off the record — but a few dozen mechanics are written into the engine and keyed by a record id (`if (owned.has('sneak-attack'))`), where no field-stripping can reach them. This file is the INVENTORY of those ids. `scripts/trust-ledger.mjs` reads it and puts the OFF ones on `lanes.engine`; `engineLaneOff(id)` (src/rules/trustLanes.ts) is what the readers ask; `scripts/trust-lanes-check.mjs` (in `npm run verify`) goes red when the engine files grow an id-keyed lane that is not listed here.
_gatedRule: `gated: true` means the reader is routed through engineLaneOff() and applies NOTHING while the lane is off. `gated: false` is a DECISION with its reason: the gate must never touch a LIMIT, a prerequisite, prose, the recovery of a player's own recorded pick, or a chassis identity test (which subclass / class feature / chosen item the character has — plan section 1 'Chassis and display are not effects' and section 2 step 3 'classes, ancestries and backgrounds are all-on'). The line between a gated class feature and an identity one: a feature whose benefit is a NUMBER computed in code (weapon specialization, sneak attack, rage damage) is a lane; a feature read to decide WHICH chassis subsystem the character has (a spellcasting entry, a font, a school, a doctrine) is identity, and darkening it would break the chassis rather than remove a benefit.

_shapes.lanes: { id, file, kind, what, gated, why? , invisibleToGuard? } — `kind` is the WG kind the lane delivers (the vocabulary of scripts/data/trust-fields.json); the ledger turns the lane off when that kind is untrusted on EVERY bucket twin of the record — and only that: the plan's 'or its record is fully dark' half is deliberately NOT a second test, with the measurement in scripts/trust-ledger.mjs's own comment (a path-poor record like feats/inventor-dedication counts as fully dark while WG encodes three kinds on it, so the disjunction would darken a record WG implements). `invisibleToGuard` marks an entry the guard's match cannot see, with the reason.
_shapes.registryFiles: { file, why } — a src/rules file whose record ids come from a TABLE rather than a hard-coded lane. Its ids are gated (or knowingly not) by the lane that owns the table, so listing them one by one here would say nothing.
_shapes.notIds: { id, why } — a word that IS a core.json record id and is also an ordinary value in the engine ('weapon' the itemType, 'medium' the size). Excluded from the match so it cannot bury the real lanes.
